source_text: πλὴν οὐ σεσίγηκεν ὁ Μωσῆς, καίτοι διᾴττοντος ἤδη πρὸς τὰ τῆς ἱερωσύνης ἔργα τοῦ Ἀαρών. Χρόνος γὰρ δὴ τῆς ἱερωσύνης Χριστοῦ νοοῖτ' ἂν εἰκότως ὁ μετὰ τὸν νόμον, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἡ ὀγδόη, καθ' ἣν ἡ ἀνάστασις, καὶ ἀρχή τις ὥσπερ αἰῶνος νέου. Καινὴ γὰρ κτίσις ἐν Χριστῷ, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. Ἀναδεδειγμένου δὲ ἤδη Χριστοῦ κατὰ τὴν ὀγδόην, καταλήγει μὲν τὰ Μωσέως· οὐ γὰρ ἐν τύποις ἔτι καὶ σκιαῖς λατρεύομεν· ἥ γε μὴν ἐννόμῳ παίδευσις οὐ σεσίγηκε, πνευματικὸς γὰρ ὁ νόμος τοῖς πνευματικοῖς, καὶ ἀεὶ τὸ Χριστοῦ λαλεῖ μυστήριον. Ἐπηγγέλλετο μὲν οὖν ὁ Μωσῆς κατὰ τὴν ὀγδόην ἡμέραν ὀφθήσεσθαι τὴν δόξαν Κυρίου. Προαναπεφώνηκε γὰρ ὁ νόμος τῆς τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἐπιδημίας τὸν χρόνον. Προσεπιτάττει δὲ πάλιν, πρότερον μὲν ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ τὸν Ἀαρὼν θυσίας ἐπιτελεῖν· μετὰ δὲ τοῦτο, τὰς ὑπὲρ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ, τύπον, οἶμαι, τὸ χρῆμα τιθεὶς τοῖς καθ' ἡμᾶς ἤδη πως, καὶ ὑποφαίνων εὖ μάλα καὶ σαφῶς, ὅτι τοῖς ἐξειλεγμένοις εἰς ἱερωσύνην, καὶ τοῖς τὸν ἐν πίστει δεχομένοις ἁγιασμὸν, πρέποι ἂν εἰκότως τὸ ἁγίους τε εἶναι καὶ ἱερούς. Τίς δ' ἂν γένοιτο τῆς προσαγωγῆς ὁ τρόπος, ὡς ἔνι δηλώσομεν. Μοσχάριον οὖν ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας καὶ καθαρισμοῦ τῶν ἱερουργούντων ἐσφάζετο. Προχεομένου δὲ τοῦ αἵματος τῷ ἁγίῳ θυσιαστηρίῳ, τεθυμιαμένων δὲ καὶ τῶν ἐντοσθίων, πυρὶ τὸ ἐπίλοιπον κατεφλέγετο σῶμα. Κριὸς δὲ δὴ πάλιν τὸ ὁλοκαυτούμενον ἦν, κατά γε τὸν συνήθη νόμον τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως· χίμαρος δὲ τὸ θῦμα πρὸς ἀποκάθαρσιν ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ· μοσχάριον δὲ καὶ ἀμνὸς, τὰ εἰς ὁλοκαύτωσιν, κριός τε καὶ μόσχος εἰς θυσίαν σωτηρίου, ἐπιτεθειμένης τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ καὶ τῆς σεμιδάλεως, εἰ καὶ μὴ πάσης τυχὸν, ἀλλὰ δρακὸς καὶ ἐκ μέρους. Εἶτά φησιν, ὅτι «Καὶ ἐξάρας Ἀαρὼν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τὸν λαὸν, ηὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς, καὶ κατέβη ποιήσας τὸ περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, καὶ τὰ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ τὰ τοῦ σωτηρίου, καὶ εἰσῆλθε Μωσῆς καὶ Ἀαρὼν εἰς τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου, καὶ ἐξελθόντες εὐλόγησαν ἅπαντα τὸν λαὸν, καὶ ὤφθη ἡ δόξα Κυρίου παντὶ τῷ λαῷ, καὶ ἐξῆλθε πῦρ παρὰ Κυρίου, καὶ κατέφαγε τὰ ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, τά τε ὁλοκαυτώματα, καὶ τὰ στέατα, καὶ εἶδε πᾶς ὁ λαὸς, καὶ ἐξέστη, καὶ ἔπεσον ἐπὶ πρόσωπον.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τί δὴ οὖν ἄρα καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖσδε φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Ὤφθη μὲν οὖν κατά γε τὸ ἀληθὲς ἡ δόξα Κυρίου κατὰ τὴν ὀγδόην, ἤτοι γέγονεν ἐμφανὴς ὁ Υἱὸς, ἡ δόξα τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός· ὠνόμαζε γὰρ αὐτὸν οὕτω λέγων πρὸς Μωσέα τὸν ἱερώτατον· «Ζῶ ἐγὼ, λέγει Κύριος, ἢ μὴν ἐμπλησθήσεται τῆς δόξης Κυρίου πᾶσα ἡ γῆ.» Ἱεροὺς δὲ ἡμᾶς ἀποφαίνει αὐτὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ὡς ἔν γε τῷ μόσχῳ σφαζόμενος, καὶ ἁμαρτίας ἐλευθερῶν, καὶ παντὸς ἀνιεὶς ἐγκλήματος, καὶ τὸν ἐκ τοῦ κατεγνῶσθαι διασμήχων ῥύπον, καὶ αὐτὸς ὁμοίως εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας τῆς νοητῆς ὡς κριὸς τελειούμενος, αὐτὸς καὶ θυσία σωτηρίου γινόμενος, καὶ ἁγιάζων ἡμᾶς τῷ ἰδίῳ αἵματι, αὐτὸς καὶ σεμίδαλις ἐλαιόδευτος, ἐν ἱλαρότητι ζωῆς ἁγίας, παραδεικνὺς ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί.
pass_a_gloss: [continues 21: 'Aaron begins,'] but Moses has not been silent (σιγάω, pf. σεσίγηκεν), though Aaron is already darting (διᾴττω) toward the works of priesthood (ἱερωσύνη). For the time (χρόνος) of Christ's priesthood would fittingly be understood as the one after the law (νόμος), that is, the eighth (ὀγδόη), on which the resurrection (ἀνάστασις), and a beginning (ἀρχή) as it were of a new age (αἰὼν νέος). For new creation (καινὴ κτίσις) in Christ, according to what is written. Christ having now been shown forth (ἀναδείκνυμι) on the eighth, the things of Moses cease (καταλήγω); for no longer in types (τύπος) and shadows (σκιά) do we worship (λατρεύω); yet the lawful instruction (ἔννομος παίδευσις) has not been silent, for the law is spiritual (πνευματικός) to the spiritual, and always speaks (λαλέω) the mystery (μυστήριον) of Christ. Moses announced (ἐπαγγέλλομαι) that on the eighth day the glory of the Lord (δόξα Κυρίου) would be seen (ὁράω, fut. pass.). For the law proclaimed beforehand (προαναφωνέω) the time of our Savior's sojourn/coming (ἐπιδημία). He further commands (προσεπιτάσσω) Aaron first to complete sacrifices (θυσία) for himself, after this those for all the people (λαός), setting the thing, I think, as a type for those of our time already somehow, and indicating (ὑποφαίνω) well and clearly that for those elected (ἐκλέγω) to priesthood, and those receiving the sanctification (ἁγιασμός) in faith (πίστις), it would fittingly befit to be holy (ἅγιος) and sacred/consecrated (ἱερός). What the manner (τρόπος) of the offering (προσαγωγή) would be, we will show as is possible. A young calf (μοσχάριον) for sin (ἁμαρτία) and cleansing (καθαρισμός) of those performing the rites (ἱερουργέω) was slaughtered (σφάζω). The blood (αἷμα) being poured forth (προχέω) at the holy altar (θυσιαστήριον), the entrails (ἐντόσθια) having been burned as smoke-offering (θυμιάω), the remaining body was burned up (καταφλέγω) by fire. A ram (κριός) again was the thing wholly burnt (ὁλοκαυτόω), according to the customary law of whole burnt offering (ὁλοκαύτωσις); a male goat (χίμαρος) the victim (θῦμα) for purging (ἀποκάθαρσις) the sin of the people; a young calf and a lamb (ἀμνός) those for whole burnt offering; a ram and a calf (μόσχος) for sacrifice of salvation (θυσία σωτηρίου), the fine flour (σεμίδαλις) also placed on the altar, if perhaps not all, but a handful (δράξ) and in part. Then it says: 'And Aaron having lifted (ἐξαίρω) the hands upon the people blessed (εὐλογέω) them, and came down having made the [offering] for sin, and the whole burnt offerings and those of salvation; and Moses and Aaron went into the tent of witness (σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου), and having come out blessed all the people, and the glory of the Lord was seen by all the people, and fire went out from the Lord and devoured (κατεσθίω) the things on the altar, the whole burnt offerings and the fats (στέαρ), and all the people saw and were astonished (ἐξίστημι) and fell on face.' PALL: What then do you say upon these? CYR: The glory of the Lord was seen according to truth on the eighth, that is, the Son became manifest (ἐμφανής), the glory of God and Father; for he named him thus saying to the most sacred Moses: 'I live, says the Lord, truly all the earth will be filled with the glory of the Lord.' He himself shows us forth (ἀποφαίνω) as sacred (ἱερός), being slaughtered for us as in the calf, and freeing from sin, and releasing (ἀνίημι) from every charge (ἔγκλημα), and scouring off (διασμήχω) the filth (ῥύπος) from being condemned (καταγινώσκω); and he likewise being perfected (τελειόω) as a ram unto an odor of sweet smell (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας) that is intelligible/spiritual (νοητός); he also becoming sacrifice of salvation, and sanctifying (ἁγιάζω) us by his own blood; he also fine flour moistened with oil (ἐλαιόδευτος), in cheerfulness (ἱλαρότης) of holy life, presenting (παραδείκνυμι) himself for us to God and Father.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …yet Moses has not fallen silent, even though Aaron is already hurrying to the works of the priesthood. For the time of Christ's priesthood may rightly be understood as the time after the law, that is, the eighth day, on which the resurrection took place, and which is, as it were, the beginning of a new age. For in Christ there is a new creation, as it is written (2 Corinthians 5:17). Once Christ has been revealed on the eighth day, the things of Moses come to an end, for we no longer worship in types and shadows (Hebrews 8:5). Yet the teaching of the law has not fallen silent, for the law is spiritual to those who are spiritual (Romans 7:14), and it always speaks of the mystery of Christ. Moses, then, promised that on the eighth day the glory of the Lord would be seen (Leviticus 9:1–6), for the law announced beforehand the time of our Savior's coming. Again he gives a further command: Aaron is first to offer sacrifices for himself, and after this those for the whole people (Leviticus 9:7). In this, I think, he already makes the matter in some way a type for those of our own day, and indicates very well and clearly that it is right and fitting for those chosen for the priesthood, and for those who receive sanctification in faith, to be holy and consecrated. What the manner of the offering was, we shall explain as best we can. A young calf, then, was slaughtered for sin and for the cleansing of those who performed the sacred rites. Its blood was poured out at the holy altar, the inner parts were turned to smoke, and the rest of the body was burned up with fire (Leviticus 9:8–11). A ram, in turn, was what was burned whole, according to the customary law of the whole burnt offering (Leviticus 9:12–14). A male goat was the victim for cleansing the people's sin (Leviticus 9:15); a young calf and a lamb were for the whole burnt offering (Leviticus 9:3, 16); a ram and a calf were for the sacrifice of salvation (Leviticus 9:4, 18), and fine flour was also laid on the altar, though perhaps not all of it, only a handful, a part of it (Leviticus 9:17). Then it says: ‘And Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them; and he came down after making the sin offering, the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifices of salvation. And Moses and Aaron went into the tent of witness, and they came out and blessed all the people; and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people. And fire came out from the Lord and consumed what was on the altar, both the whole burnt offerings and the fat portions; and all the people saw it, and were amazed, and fell on their faces’ (Leviticus 9:22–24).
Palladius: What, then, do you say about this as well?

Cyril: In truth the glory of the Lord was seen on the eighth day; that is, the Son, the glory of God the Father, became manifest. For God named him so when he said to the most holy Moses, ‘As I live, says the Lord, all the earth shall surely be filled with the glory of the Lord’ (Numbers 14:21). It is he himself who makes us consecrated. He is slain for us, like the calf; he sets us free from sin, releases us from every charge, and scours away the filth that comes from being condemned. He likewise, like the ram, is made perfect for a pleasing spiritual aroma; he himself becomes the sacrifice of salvation and sanctifies us with his own blood (Hebrews 13:12); he himself is the fine flour moistened with oil, in the gladness of a holy life, presenting himself for us to God the Father (Ephesians 5:2).
